answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the orchard check immediately, the ivory audit keeps the resolved set and the harbor replay exposes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 105 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 105 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. That is 26 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
